scientific_name: Fuchsia x hybrida 'Sun Pendants Hot Pink'

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed into containers or beds in partial to full shade; this compact, mounded-to-semi-trailing fuchsia was bred for stronger heat tolerance than older fuchsia hybrids.

directions: Plant in a shaded or part-shaded container, hanging basket, or window box in moist, well-drained soil, since this low, mounded fuchsia stays small and performs best out of hot direct sun. It hangs dangling, hot-pink, magenta-throated flowers continuously from planting until frost without any deadheading, since spent blooms drop cleanly and few seeds form. Water regularly to keep the shallow root zone from drying out, and feed lightly through the season to sustain nonstop bloom. Its compact, trailing-mounded habit suits small pots and basket edges better than large landscape beds.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants in part sun to full sun in rich, well-drained soil; Aromance Plum Honey carries the largest, most fragrant flowers yet in the Aromance series and blooms heaviest during cool spring and fall weather.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in part to full sun, giving it room to mound and spread since it grows noticeably wider than tall. Its oversized, sweetly scented flowers blend plum-purple with cream and soft yellow, covering the compact plant most heavily in cool weather, and improved heat tolerance keeps it flowering further into summer than older nemesia types before slowing in sustained heat. No deadheading is needed since it is self-cleaning; a light trim after a hot spell encourages fresh rebloom as temperatures ease. Feed yearly with compost or fertilizer to keep the display dense in containers, window boxes, and border edges.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all danger of frost in full sun and average, well-drained soil; Vanilla Breeze is a well-branched, spreading Luscious-series lantana suited to mass plantings and large containers.

directions: Plant in full sun in average, well-drained soil, where this vigorous, well-branched lantana spreads as wide as it grows tall. Fragrant flower clusters open soft buttery yellow and age to creamy white, giving each cluster a two-tone look that holds continuously from planting through hard frost without deadheading, since the plant sets few to no seeds. It tolerates heat and drought once established and performs best when allowed to dry between waterings rather than kept constantly moist. In zone 9 expect it to die back in a hard freeze and resprout from the root system the following spring.

common_name: Sweet Caroline Bewitched After Midnight II Ornamental Sweet Potato Vine

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated transplants after all frost danger has passed into containers or beds in part sun to full sun; this improved selection holds deep purple-black foliage color better in extreme heat than earlier dark-leaved sweet potato vines.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in part sun to full sun, giving it room to mound before it spills over container edges, since its habit is more upright and mounded than the strictly trailing habit of older sweet potato vine selections. Foliage holds a deep, glossy purple-black color through summer heat that only loses a little intensity toward olive-purple in the most extreme conditions, and colors stay richest with more direct sun. It weaves naturally among taller companion plants in mixed containers and needs only routine feeding and water to perform all season without pinching. Grow it strictly as a warm-season annual outside zone 10-11, since it has no frost tolerance.
